items.title: How much sticky sessions actually protect you as the cluster grows
items.description: With sticky sessions, each active login is pinned to exactly one server. When the autoscaler removes a server, every session pinned to it is lost — roughly an even 1-in-N share of all active sessions, since routing spreads users evenly across N servers. Drag the server count to see how that share shrinks (but never reaches zero) as the cluster grows.

items.title: How adding claims grows a JWT's size on the wire
items.description: Every JWT pays a fixed cost (header + base fields like sub/iat/exp + signature) plus roughly 20 raw bytes per extra claim (a role flag, a tenant ID) — then base64url expands all of that by about 4/3. This reproduces the token-byte-size exercises above: 0 extra claims is 133 bytes, 5 is 267. Drag the claim count to see how quickly a 'just add one more field' habit adds up, especially for a token sent on every single request.
